issues.description: req.stream vs req.bounded_stream swap silently changes time/value semantics without explanation
issues.detail: The change from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() in things_advanced.py is the load-bearing semantic edit, but it's buried under a test-addition PR. These are not the same value: req.stream is the raw WSGI input (read may block or over-read), req.bounded_stream is bounded by Content-Length. That's the actual fact about the world this code now represents, and it deserves to be named, not slipped in. COMPLECTED: a behavior fix is intertwined with a test-coverage commit.

issues.description: FAQ example complects three concerns: header override, empty-body semantics, and Content-Length trust
issues.detail: The new FAQ snippet teaches 'how to set headers in tests' by way of a handler that reads req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) and branches on truthiness. That mixes the value (the bytes), the identity (the stream position), and the time (when the read returns) into a single conditional. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: it answers 'how do I override a header' with a worked example that itself models a subtle bug. A reader copying this pattern will inherit the conflation. The FAQ should show only the header override and link separately to the empty-body semantics question.

issues.description: Test asserts behavior of a contradiction (empty body, Content-Length: 1) without naming what the framework promises
issues.detail: resp4 sends body='' with Content-Length: '1' and asserts status 400. That's a useful test, but it is testing what bounded_stream.read() returns when the declared length exceeds the actual body. The test passes because read() returns empty and the handler raises HTTPBadRequest. The fact being asserted (that falcon's bounded_stream surfaces truncation as an empty read, not an exception or a hang) is not stated anywhere. INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY: the test couples example behavior to an undocumented framework promise. Either document the promise or assert it directly against bounded_stream, not transitively through the example.

issues.description: README diff mixes formatting churn with two real semantic edits
issues.detail: The README changes contain (a) cosmetic reformatting of multi-line strings and imports, (b) a signature change to StorageError.handle (ex, req, resp, params) -> (req, resp, ex, params), and (c) a switch from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read(). Items (b) and (c) are facts about the API contract; item (a) is incidental. COMPLECTED commit: mixing whitespace-grade edits with behavior changes makes the diff harder to reason about and the history harder to bisect. Split the cosmetic from the semantic.

issues.description: The handler still complects 'is there a body' with 'is the body well-formed JSON'
issues.detail: JSONTranslator.process_request reads the stream, checks `if not body`, then tries json.loads. Three distinct facts (declared length, actual bytes, parseable JSON) are tangled in one function with three different error paths. The PR doesn't make this worse, but the bug that motivated it (empty body with non-zero Content-Length) is a symptom of this tangling. The simpler decomposition: one function returns the bytes (or a typed 'truncated' value), another parses. Not blocking for this PR, but worth naming because the fix here patches a symptom of the underlying complecting.

review.summary: This PR is presented as a test addition but smuggles a real semantic change: req.stream.read() becomes req.bounded_stream.read() in the example, and the test it adds only passes because of that swap. The two should be separated and the bounded_stream choice named for what it is (a different value with different time semantics under truncated bodies). The FAQ addition is well-intentioned but the worked example complects header override with a handler that itself conflates declared length, actual bytes, and parse success, which is exactly the kind of "easy" pattern readers will copy. The test asserts an undocumented framework promise (bounded_stream returns empty on Content-Length mismatch) transitively through the example rather than directly. None of this is P0, but the PR would be simpler and more honest as two commits: one for the bounded_stream fix with a direct framework-level test, one for the FAQ and example-coverage tests.
